text:
maria: Heads up — p95 latency for hosted-chat in us-west-2 spiked to ~1.8s around 10:12 UTC. GPU queue_depth climbed past 220 and streaming requests were starved while long non-stream jobs kept slots. digging logs and posting a quick proposal. :eyes:
jordan: I saw that alert. traces show a lot of streaming connections holding KV cache open for long rerank/batch-compute calls. head-of-line blocking.
saul: Proposal: introduce a streamslot allocator that reserves a small number of cheap, preemptible "stream slots" per GPU. semantics: short leases, idle timeout, preemptible on priority. This prevents requests that need interactive streaming from waiting behind long non-stream GPU jobs.
maria: can you sketch config? want to understand tradeoffs with batching and throughput.
saul: example config (pseudo-yaml):
```
gpu:
  stream_slots_per_gpu: 6
  stream_slot_idle_ms: 1500
  preempt_grace_ms: 200
  non_stream_pool_concurrency: 40
  allow_opportunistic_spill: true
```
behavior: stream requests get assigned a slot lease; if none free, they enter fast queue with short timeout. non-stream jobs use shared pool and are preemptible if a high-priority stream arrives (eviction with graceful finish window).
jordan: main tradeoff is batching efficiency. reserving slots reduces batch depth => cost up. but tail latency improves. We saw canary numbers show p95 down ~300ms, throughput for heavy batch work dropped ~2-3%.
maria: cost note: preliminary estimate says dedicated GPU minutes up ~7% for the canary in usw2 because batching is less efficient. need to weigh SLO benefit vs $ impact.
jordan: alternative: token-budgeted admission control per API key. give streaming callers a small long-pollen budget; when fleet saturation hits thresholds, throttle token budgets rather than hard slot gating. less strict preemption, preserves batching for heavy customers.
saul: we can combine: stream slots + token budgets. stream slots for extreme low-latency interactive flows, token budgets to shape noisy clients. metrics to track: stream_slot_util, stream_wait_time_seconds, nonstream_batch_size, preempt_count, token_throttle_rate. prom queries:
```
sum(rate(stream_wait_time_seconds_sum[5m])) / sum(rate(stream_wait_time_seconds_count[5m]))
sum(gpu_queue_depth) by (region)
```
opsbot: Canary deploy: streamslot allocator v1 -> prod-usw2 canary at 10:40 UTC (route: 5% traffic). initial metrics: streaming p95 -300ms, non-stream batch throughput -2%, preempt_count=38 over 20m. :rocket:
maria: good start. what's the rollback threshold? we should define a runbook trigger.
jordan: runbook: if streaming p95 > 800ms OR non-stream error_rate > 0.5% OR preempt_count spikes > 200/min, rollback to previous routing within 5m.
saul: ops-wise, we need graceful eviction: don't kill running non-stream mid-token. send a SIG to let them flush for preempt_grace_ms then checkpoint. Also add a flag to allow opportunistic spillover: if non-stream pool has spare cycles, allow streams to borrow for N seconds. that reduces cost impact.
maria: rollout plan: 5% -> monitor 30m -> 25% -> 60m -> 100% if SLOs hold. I'll lead the rollout and own the dashboards. SLO targets: streaming p95 < 700ms; non-stream error_rate < 0.5%; cost change tracked as % GPU-minute delta. :thumbsup:
jordan: also experiment A/B: slot gating vs token-budgeting. prefer token-budgeting for lower-tier customers to avoid paying extra for reserved slots. add feature-flag toggle.
opsbot: /ff set streamslot_opportunistic true --env prod-usw2 acknowledged at 10:52 UTC.
maria: ok, I'll wire dashboard panels now (stream_wait_time, gpu_queue_depth, preempt_count, token_throttle_rate) and ping infra to adjust autoscaling headroom if needed. :eyes:
jordan: quick note — region constraints: us-east has higher batch-heavy traffic; tune stream_slots_per_gpu lower there (3) to preserve batch efficiency. usw2 we keep 6.
saul: recording follow-ups: implement preempt grace checkpoint, add admission control hook in front of router, run cost sim for 7 days of traffic with streamslot enabled to estimate $ impact.
maria: thanks team. will post canary update in 30m. :coffee:
